# Recorded audio QA fixtures

These are actual human recordings, not oscillator simulations. Tests explicitly separate annotated pitch accuracy, sustained-note input robustness, browser capture transport and song playback. Fixtures are excluded from the web build.

- **vocadito_1**: 33.21 s, Filipino “Ako ay may lobo”. Audio, F0, two note annotations and lyrics from vocadito (2021), Rachel Bittner, Katherine Pasalo, Juan José Bosch, Gabriel Meseguer Brocal and David Rubinstein. CC-BY-4.0. https://zenodo.org/records/5578807 . Retrieved from mirdata's official test resources. F0 is an independent annotation, not generated by this app. Only this excerpt of the forty-recording corpus is included/tested.
- **martin-*.wav**: 20 sustained human notes from vocobox/human-voice-dataset. MIT; see LICENSE.human-voice-dataset. Filenames give intended notes, not independent F0 truth; tests do not infer accuracy from these filenames. https://github.com/vocobox/human-voice-dataset
- **Let's Go Fishin'**, Karissa Hobbs: vocal + guitar recording published under CC-BY-3.0; exact attribution is in Karissa_Hobbs_-_Lets_Go_Fishin.txt. https://github.com/librosa/data . The controlled JSON note used in the transport test is not claimed to be this song's original melody.

manifest.json records source URLs, sizes and SHA-256 hashes. Run node scripts/fetch-audio-fixtures.mjs to reproduce the downloads. Chromium's fake audio device replays the real vocadito recording through getUserMedia; it is not a physical live-singer test.
